commit.message: fix(web): restore full browser Back and Forward history (#65)

specification.objective: Complete issue 65 web browser history so Back and Forward restore canonical URL and corresponding screen, while preserving all locked v1 navigation and authentication invariants.

requirements.statement: When navigating through workspace routes A to B to C, Back restores B then A, and Forward restores B then C in a real browser, with URL and content synchronized.
Navigating to the active named route does not add entries, and new navigation after Back truncates only the browser forward branch naturally.
The six existing named workspace URLs and direct deep links work; reload and navigation transitions retain session bootstrap, error/retry, forced password change and unauthenticated guards.
Login/registration install a canonical route; logout clears the session and browser Back/Forward cannot re-expose protected content; dialog navigation remains functional.
The 19 versioned POLIS contracts at commit 9d61bfe, including locked browser-navigation-history-issue-65-v1, remain unchanged; archive a new locked v6 contract for this follow-up.

acceptance_criteria.statement: Widget and Chrome tests exercise A-B-C-Back-Back-Forward-Forward and compare route URL with rendered content.
Tests verify repeated active destination does not add entries and replacing a forward branch preserves normal browser semantics.
All six authenticated deep links, startup session errors/retry, revoked/expired session, mandatory password change and anonymous login remain guarded.
Authenticated login/registration URLs are canonical and logout does not expose earlier protected content through Back/Forward.
POLIS strict development evidence passes with the new locked contract and all 19 prior contract bytes remain identical to HEAD baseline.

invariants.statement: Retain existing authentication and role selection rules, route names, visible screens, theme and backend interfaces.
Preserve previous v1 locked POLIS contract bytes and all other committed POLIS contracts.
Use Flutter Router/Navigator APIs for bidirectional browser history without manually inserting JavaScript history records or adding dependencies.

forbidden_states.statement: Forward returns null or stays on A after A-B-Back.
URL changes but screen does not, or screen changes without the matching URL.
Logout or revoked session can be bypassed through browser Back/Forward.
Duplicate menu selections create phantom history entries.

inputs.statement: Browser Back and Forward, primary drawer navigation, deep links, login/registration/logout.

outputs.statement: Synchronized canonical route and view in browser navigation history.
Versioned follow-up POLIS locked contract and regression tests.

failure_semantics.statement: Without a declarative Router, the new regression test fails and prints browser_forward_history_missing.

argv: import subprocess,sys; p=subprocess.run(['flutter','test','test/core/navigation/browser_history_test.dart','--plain-name','browser router supports bidirectional history'],cwd='frontend'); print('browser_forward_history_missing' if p.returncode else 'browser_forward_history_present'); sys.exit(p.returncode)
